issue_context.title: [System.Text.Json] Regression: [JsonIgnore] Attribute not Applied to Ref Returns
issue_context.body:
### Description

Found a regression in `System.Text.Json` where using properties with `ref returns` cannot be ignored for serialization, leading to an unavoidable exception.

Regression was introduced in `System.Text.Json 6.0.0-rc.1.21406.5`, going by the available packages in the `dotnet6` NuGet repo. This package was pushed on Friday, August 6th, 2021.

As I'm not familiar with how dotnet is exactly built, I do not know how to pinpoint the sdk build number to the exact commit causing the issue however; but the build version should hopefully be useful.

Minimal Reproduction:
```csharp
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

var sampleText = new TypeWithRefString();
var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(sampleText); // Exception Here
var deserialized = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<TypeWithRefString>(json); // And Here

internal class TypeWithRefString
{
    [JsonIgnore]
    public ref string NameRef => ref Name;
    public string Name = "How many Richard Landers does it take to write a blog entry? Just one, you rock!";
}
```

Debug in your own desired way. 
This snippet can be pasted and ran over a blank .NET 6 console app. 

### Configuration

N/A

### Regression?

Yes, this use case worked with any version of System.Text.Json <= `6.0.0-rc.1.21406.4`;

### Other information

Exception:
```csharp
System.ArgumentException: 'The type 'System.String&' may not be used as a type argument.'
   at System.RuntimeType.ThrowIfTypeNeverValidGenericArgument(RuntimeType type)
   at System.RuntimeType.SanityCheckGenericArguments(RuntimeType[] genericArguments, RuntimeType[] genericParamters)
   at System.RuntimeType.MakeGenericType(Type[] instantiation)
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Converters.ObjectConverterFactory.CreateConverter(Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonConverterFactory.GetConverterInternal(Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetConverterInternal(Type typeToConvert)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.DetermineConverter(Type parentClassType, Type runtimePropertyType, MemberInfo memberInfo)
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo.GetConverter(Type type, Type parentClassType, MemberInfo memberInfo, Type& runtimeType, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo.AddProperty(MemberInfo memberInfo, Type memberType, Type parentClassType, Boolean isVirtual, Nullable`1 parentTypeNumberHandling, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo.CacheMember(Type declaringType, Type memberType, MemberInfo memberInfo, Boolean isVirtual, Nullable`1 typeNumberHandling, Boolean& propertyOrderSpecified, Dictionary`2& ignoredMembers)
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo..ctor(Type type, JsonConverter converter, Type runtimeType, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo..ctor(Type type, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.<RootBuiltInConvertersAndTypeInfoCreator>g__CreateJsonTypeInfo|107_0(Type type, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetClassFromContextOrCreate(Type type)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetOrAddClass(Type type)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetOrAddClassForRootType(Type type)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.GetTypeInfo(Type runtimeType, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Write[TValue](TValue& value, Type runtimeType, JsonSerializerOptions options)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize[TValue](TValue value, JsonSerializerOptions options)
```

Can repro -- I believe this is the same regression as the one reported in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/58469#issuecomment-920977360. 

We made the call earlier not to revert the change, but it seems to me that this particular issue makes a more compelling case /cc @layomia 

Related to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/59364.
Ha! I'll be writing the RC2 post this week.
Re-opening so we can consider porting the fix to .NET 6.0.

review_comments: Given that this only used once in conjunction with `GetParamDefaultValueAsString`, would it make sense to meld the two into a single method. It might more clearly communicate how `ParameterInfo` are mapped to argument expressions.

It's also used in the reflection serializer here - https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/b39f6bf98b929b32c3cdd3e6add7bd8b746ea2ca/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/Metadata/JsonTypeInfo.cs#L533.
Ah ok, hadn't realized it was shared file.

Out of curiosity, why does this throw `InvalidOperationException` when the previous was throwing `ArgumentException`? It would seem to me that both should be surfacing `InvalidOperationException`, unless that's a breaking change we cannot make.

It's two different exceptions for two different scenarios: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/59936 (ref property, `ArgumentException`) and https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/58469 (invalid converter type, `InvalidOperationException`). `ArgumentException` is thrown when passing `System.String&` as a generic parameter type to `MakeGenericType` deep in our internals. We've had behavior like this since 3.0 (see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/34777 and related issues). Changing exception type is not a breaking change, but I think it is out of scope for this PR to go from `ArgumentException` to `InvalidOperationException`since the focus of this PR is to address the `[JsonIgnore]` regression.

Ref prop support is something we should consider supporting perhaps as part of https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/34779, given it's currently supported in src-gen - https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ffb733f17be91923a0dc8f19d6fa4bf65cf013f9/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/tests/Common/PropertyVisibilityTests.cs#L2759-L2768.
Could you also add a comment here explaining why `sbyte` is being used?
Will be sure to do so in a follow up to avoid CI reset. It will be the same as the comment on `CreateIgnoredParameterPlaceholder` below.
What happens when attempting to serialize these types in source gen? Are we testing for that?

Yes we are testing for that on L2758-2785. When `[JsonIgnore]` is not applied: source gen supports the ref return case, but falls back to a built in converter in the invalid converter config case (opened https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/60020 to address this).

When `[JsonIgnore]` is applied, source gen and reflection have the same behavior of not throwing.
I'm slightly confused by these tests. Do they related to fixing #59936?

Yes they are. Now that the `T`s for `JsonPropertyInfo<T>` instances  matching constructor parameters have been reverted from the actual property type to `sbyte` (to fix the `[JsonIgnore]` regression), we can no longer use those `T`s to retrieve the default values for ctor params (needed when invoking the ctor and there is no matching JSON, or the matching prop has been ignored). This PR adds replacement logic to get the needed default values. These tests were added to further exercise this new logic (in addition to existing ctor tests to ensure no known regressions).
Was this an issue before? Is there a test for this (a struct-based parameter not specified in JSON)?

Yes this was an issue now fixed in this PR (out of necessity). Tests were initially added but removed from this PR to keep the diff limited to the major scenario reported. I've re-added them in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/60024/commits/f9f702fb9a422a8b6fee6e5daca7a921110fe53e since there are related product changes.
The new generic-method-holder changes were added for this test scenario to pass rather than have a NullReferenceException due to casts from null to value types.
Is the `InfoVarName` refactoring necessary? Given we're backporting this to GA branch I would try to keep the diff to the essential changes. We can improve in `main` in future iterations.
